item.title: [Injury] Brandin Podziemski (GSW): Brandin Podziemski (back) is questionable for Friday’s game against the Grizzlies.
item.description:
Brandin Podziemski (back) is questionable for Friday’s game against the Grizzlies.

Podziemski did not play in Wednesday’s loss to the Lakers, leading to De’Anthony Melton taking the starting spot. Melton played 21 minutes, while reserves Will Richard and Brandon Williams played 20 and 18 minutes, respectively. Expect a similar rotation if Podziemski can’t play on Friday.

Raphielle Johnson

Fonte: NBA Injury Report

item.title: [Injury] Isaiah Stewart (MEM): Isaiah Stewart (ankle) is questionable for Friday’s game against the Warriors.
item.description:
Isaiah Stewart (ankle) is questionable for Friday’s game against the Warriors.

Stewart, injured during the preseason, did not play in Wednesday’s win over the Jazz. Quinten Post logged 19 minutes off the bench as the backup center, and he’ll likely keep that role if Beef Stew can’t play on Friday.

Raphielle Johnson

Fonte: NBA Injury Report

item.title: [Injury] Cedric Coward (MEM): Cedric Coward (wrist) is doubtful for Friday’s game against the Warriors.
item.description:
Cedric Coward (wrist) is doubtful for Friday’s game against the Warriors.

Coward, who played 28 minutes in Wednesday’s win over the Jazz, is dealing with a sprained left wrist. With the doubtful tag, he’s more likely to miss Friday. If Coward sits, reserves like Scotty Pippen Jr. and Jerami Grant would get more offensive opportunities.

Raphielle Johnson

Fonte: NBA Injury Report

item.title: [Injury] Bradley Beal (LAC): Bradley Beal (knee) is out for Friday’s game against the Lakers.
item.description:
Bradley Beal (knee) is out for Friday’s game against the Lakers.

Beal will miss a second straight game due to right knee injury management. Kobe Sanders and Gradey Dick played rotation minutes off the bench in Wednesday’s win over the Kings, with the latter scoring 12 points in 19 minutes. Look for more of the same on Friday night.

Raphielle Johnson

Fonte: NBA Injury Report

item.title: [Injury] Charles Bassey (GSW): Charles Bassey (knee) is questionable for Friday’s game against the Grizzlies.
item.description:
Charles Bassey (knee) is questionable for Friday’s game against the Grizzlies.

Bassey did not play in Wednesday’s opener against the Lakers, leaving the Warriors light on options at center. With Kristaps Porziņģis (illness) out indefinitely, Draymond Green may spend more time at center than head coach Steve Kerr would prefer. Al Horford can provide depth off the bench, but he’s unlikely to exceed 20 minutes.

Raphielle Johnson

item.title: [Injury] Spencer Jones (DEN): Spencer Jones (hamstring) is out for Thursday’s game against the Thunder.
item.description:
Spencer Jones (hamstring) is out for Thursday’s game against the Thunder.

Jones, who strained his left hamstring early in training camp, is also navigating a right hamstring injury. His absence may give fellow reserve Trevon Brazile a few minutes, but it is unlikely to significantly affect fantasy basketball.

Raphielle Johnson

item.title: [Injury] Collin Sexton (LAL): Collin Sexton (leg) is not on the injury report for Friday’s game against the Clippers.
item.description:
Collin Sexton (leg) is not on the injury report for Friday’s game against the Clippers.

Sexton didn’t play in the preseason or the Lakers’ season-opening win over the Warriors, so the Lakers may monitor his minutes closely on Friday. Getting him back gives JJ Redick another option off the bench, which lacks on-ball playmakers.

item.title: [Injury] Jake LaRavia (LAL): Jake LaRavia (ankle) is questionable for Friday’s game against the Clippers.
item.description:
Jake LaRavia (ankle) is questionable for Friday’s game against the Clippers.

LaRavia sprained his right ankle in Wednesday’s win over the Warriors, and team trainers helped him back to the locker room. With Cameron Carr (oblique) and Adou Thiero (knee) already out, LaRavia’s minutes will likely be split among Matisse Thybulle, Ziaire Williams and Quentin Grimes if he can’t play on Friday. Despite coming off the bench, Grimes offers a higher category league ceiling than Thybulle or Williams.

Raphielle Johnson

item.description:
Cameron Carr (oblique) and Adou Thiero (knee) are out for Friday’s game against the Clippers.

Neither Carr nor Thiero played in Wednesday’s win over the Warriors, and both are considered day-to-day moving forward. Their absences mean the Lakers will stick with a nine-man rotation, with backup center Kevon Looney as the ninth man.

item.description:

Keldon Johnson (mouth) is questionable for Friday’s game against the Rockets.

Johnson suffered a laceration to his mouth during Tuesday’s loss to the Thunder, but he still played 20 minutes off the bench. He’ll likely carry a similar workload if he’s available on Friday. If Johnson can’t play, Harrison Barnes and Carter Bryant stand to gain the most in playing time.

Tobias Harris (calf) is out for Friday’s game against the Rockets.

item.title: [Injury] De'Aaron Fox (SAS): De’Aaron Fox (wrist) is questionable for Friday’s game against the Rockets.
item.description:
De’Aaron Fox (wrist) is questionable for Friday’s game against the Rockets.

Fox, who played 32 minutes in Tuesday’s season-opening loss to the Thunder, is dealing with a sprained right wrist. If there’s a silver lining to the injury, it’s that he shoots left-handed. If Fox can’t play on Friday, Julian Champagnie could move into the starting lineup after playing 30 minutes off the bench on Tuesday.

item.description:
Reed Sheppard (knee) is questionable for Friday’s game against the Spurs.

Sheppard, who logged 16 minutes off the bench in Wednesday’s win over the Mavericks, is dealing with a bone bruise and contusion in his left knee. The third-year guard is effectively third in the Rockets’ point-guard pecking order behind Fred VanVleet and Marcus Smart, which hurts his fantasy value.

Steven Adams (calf) is questionable for Friday’s game against the Spurs.

item.description:
Dailyn Swain (gastrointestinal illness) and Jordan Hawkins (gastrointestinal illness) are questionable for Friday’s game against the Bucks.

Zach Collins (quad) is probable for Friday’s game against the Bucks.

item.description:
Cavs reporter Chris Fedor reports that Jarrett Allen says he will play against the 76ers on Thursday.

Allen has been dealing with right patellar tendinopathy, but he attended Thursday’s shootaround and said that he expects to play. In three matchups with the 76ers last season, Allen averaged 14.7 points, 7.3 rebounds and 2.3 “stocks.”

item.title: [Injury] AJ Dybantsa (WAS): The Athletic’s Josh Robbins reports that AJ Dybantsa (ankle) is out for Friday’s home matchup with the Raptors.
item.description:
The Athletic’s Josh Robbins reports that AJ Dybantsa (ankle) is out for Friday’s home matchup with the Raptors.

Dybantsa will miss a second straight game due to a sprained left ankle, but the Wizards play the second leg of a back-to-back set on Saturday against the Bulls, which will give the rookie a quick turnaround to make his regular-season debut. Dybantsa could replace Bilal Coulibaly or Kyshawn George in the starting five when he finally gets back on the court.

Zak Hanshew

Fonte: Josh Robbins

item.title: [Recap] Keegan Murray (SAC): Keegan Murray accounted for two points (1-of-8 FGs), four rebounds and one steal in Wednesday’s loss to the Clippers.
item.description:
Keegan Murray accounted for two points (1-of-8 FGs), four rebounds and one steal in Wednesday’s loss to the Clippers.

Given Darius Acuff Jr.'s struggles on Wednesday, Murray’s night may avoid some scrutiny. However, he also struggled, missing his first seven attempts and not scoring until 9:08 remained in the fourth quarter. And Murray didn’t do much in the other categories either, which is a concern for fantasy managers. He’ll look to bounce back on Friday when the Kings host Portland.

Raphielle Johnson

item.title: [Recap] Darius Acuff (SAC): Darius Acuff Jr. amassed 12 points (5-of-24 FGs, 2-of-5 FTs), three rebounds, three assists and three steals in Wednesday’s loss to the Clippers.
item.description:
Darius Acuff Jr. amassed 12 points (5-of-24 FGs, 2-of-5 FTs), three rebounds, three assists and three steals in Wednesday’s loss to the Clippers.

Most fantasy managers and basketball fans expect rookie point guards to be inefficient. However, Acuff’s performance against the Clippers was rough. He missed all seven three-point attempts, shot 5-of-24 from the field, and finished with more turnovers (four) than assists (three). Acuff’s upside is undeniable, but he’ll have games like Wednesday.

Raphielle Johnson

item.title: [Recap] Domantas Sabonis (SAC): Domantas Sabonis finished Wednesday’s loss to the Clippers with 14 points (5-of-5 FGs, 4-of-4 FTs), 18 rebounds, eight assists and one steal.
item.description:
Domantas Sabonis finished Wednesday’s loss to the Clippers with 14 points (5-of-5 FGs, 4-of-4 FTs), 18 rebounds, eight assists and one steal.

Sabonis didn’t miss a shot on Wednesday and finished two assists shy of a triple-double. However, it’s fair to ask why he didn’t get more shots, especially when Darius Acuff Jr. and Keegan Murray combined to shoot 6-of-32 from the field. Playing alongside a rookie point guard can be challenging for a veteran post player like Sabonis, who can also facilitate offense. However, Wednesday’s outing showed he can offer excellent fantasy value on nights with low shot attempts.

Raphielle Johnson

item.title: [Recap] Zach LaVine (SAC): Zach LaVine recorded 28 points (10-of-19 FGs, 5-of-8 FTs), four rebounds, four assists and three three-pointers in Wednesday’s loss to the Clippers.
item.description:
Zach LaVine recorded 28 points (10-of-19 FGs, 5-of-8 FTs), four rebounds, four assists and three three-pointers in Wednesday’s loss to the Clippers.

After injuries limited him to 39 games in his first full season with the Kings, LaVine looked completely healthy on Wednesday. Without him and fellow veteran Domantas Sabonis, the Kings would have fared worse, but they still lost the opener 121-96. As long as he stays healthy, LaVine should return to being a reliable fantasy asset. The question is whether a good first half of the season would convince a contending team to acquire him before the February trade deadline.

Raphielle Johnson

item.title: [Recap] Keaton Wagler (LAC): Keaton Wagler notched 15 points (4-of-8 FGs, 4-of-4 FTs), five rebounds, five assists, two steals and three three-pointers in Wednesday’s win over the Kings.
item.description:
Keaton Wagler notched 15 points (4-of-8 FGs, 4-of-4 FTs), five rebounds, five assists, two steals and three three-pointers in Wednesday’s win over the Kings.

In a matchup of lottery picks, Wagler had a much better night than Sacramento’s Darius Acuff Jr. The former Illinois standout played 29 minutes off the bench, sharing the court with Darius Garland and taking a few short stints as the lone playmaker. Wagler was efficient, and while you shouldn’t overreact to one game, it wouldn’t hurt to add him now if he’s on the waiver wire in deep leagues.

Raphielle Johnson

item.title: [Recap] Brook Lopez (LAC): Brook Lopez accumulated 17 points (7-of-12 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), 11 rebounds, one assist, one steal, one block and one three-pointer in Wednesday’s win over the Kings.
item.description:
Brook Lopez accumulated 17 points (7-of-12 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), 11 rebounds, one assist, one steal, one block and one three-pointer in Wednesday’s win over the Kings.

Despite coming off the bench, Lopez played 27 minutes on Wednesday due to starting center Isaiah Jackson getting into foul trouble. The veteran 7-footer clearly still has something left in the tank, as he recorded a complete stat line that included a double-double. Jackson still hasn’t established himself as a center you can fully trust in fantasy basketball, which is a good reason to roster Lopez in deep leagues.

Raphielle Johnson

item.title: [Recap] Rui Hachimura (LAC): Rui Hachimura tallied 10 points (3-of-13 FGs, 2-of-5 FTs), eight rebounds, two assists, one steal, one block and two three-pointers in Wednesday’s win over the Kings.
item.description:
Rui Hachimura tallied 10 points (3-of-13 FGs, 2-of-5 FTs), eight rebounds, two assists, one steal, one block and two three-pointers in Wednesday’s win over the Kings.

Given the Clippers’ lack of proven scorers, Hachimura is in a position to offer more value than he did as a Laker. However, you have to make shots, and he didn’t do that consistently enough on Wednesday. Hachimura shot 1-of-6 from inside the arc, which hurt his field-goal percentage. He did put up decent numbers in rebounds, steals and blocked shots, so Wednesday wasn’t a total loss for those rostering Hachimura.

Raphielle Johnson

item.title: [Recap] Isaiah Jackson (LAC): Isaiah Jackson accounted for 13 points (6-of-8 FGs, 1-of-2 FTs), five rebounds and one steal in Wednesday’s win over the Kings.
item.description:
Isaiah Jackson accounted for 13 points (6-of-8 FGs, 1-of-2 FTs), five rebounds and one steal in Wednesday’s win over the Kings.

Jackson’s starting nod was expected to raise his fantasy ceiling, and he was productive Wednesday night. However, the Clippers’ center played just 15 minutes because of foul trouble. Backup Brook Lopez played 27 minutes, and that may not have happened if Jackson were able to stay on the court. Jackson is worth a look in 12-team leagues if he’s on the waiver wire, even with the foul trouble against Sacramento.

Raphielle Johnson

item.title: [Recap] Darius Garland (LAC): Darius Garland finished Wednesday’s win over the Kings with 30 points (11-of-19 FGs, 5-of-8 FTs), one rebound, four assists, one steal and three three-pointers.
item.description:
Darius Garland finished Wednesday’s win over the Kings with 30 points (11-of-19 FGs, 5-of-8 FTs), one rebound, four assists, one steal and three three-pointers.

After a tumultuous offseason for the franchise, the Clippers got their 2026-27 off to a good start on Wednesday. Garland dominated his individual matchup against Kings rookie guard Darius Acuff Jr., scoring an efficient 30 points. Matchups will get tougher as the season progresses, but fantasy managers hope Garland delivers performances of this caliber more often.

Raphielle Johnson

item.title: [Recap] Scoot Henderson (POR): Scoot Henderson accounted for 15 points (7-of-14 FGs), two rebounds, one assist, one steal and one three-pointer in Wednesday’s win over the Suns.
item.description:
Scoot Henderson accounted for 15 points (7-of-14 FGs), two rebounds, one assist, one steal and one three-pointer in Wednesday’s win over the Suns.

Among the four guards in Portland’s rotation, Henderson (19 minutes) played the least on Wednesday. He played nine of those minutes after halftime, while starters Ja Morant and Damian Lillard and reserve Jrue Holiday (8/4/1/2) logged between seven and nine minutes each. While Henderson having a role won’t be an issue for him, his playing time might be, especially against tougher opponents.

Raphielle Johnson

item.title: [Injury] Micah Potter (POR): Micah Potter (illness) is available for Wednesday’s game against the Suns.
item.description:
Micah Potter (illness) is available for Wednesday’s game against the Suns.

Potter has been dealing with an illness, but was trending in the right direction today and has been ruled in for matchup with the Suns. As merely a depth option for the Trail Blazers, Potter is unlikely to play significant minutes Wednesday.

Nick Shlain

item.description:
Deni Avdija (ankle) will start against Suns.

Stephen Curry (ankle) is available for Wednesday’s game against the Lakers.

item.title: Isaiah Jackson (LAC): Darius Garland, Kris Dunn, Derrick Jones Jr., Rui Hachimura and Isaiah Jackson will start Wednesday’s game against the Kings.
item.description:
Darius Garland, Kris Dunn, Derrick Jones Jr., Rui Hachimura and Isaiah Jackson will start Wednesday’s game against the Kings.

Dunn is good to go after missing most of the preseason with a minor injury, and he’ll start alongside Garland in the backcourt. Clippers head coach Tyronn Lue said on Saturday that Jackson would start at center, so his inclusion is unsurprising. Garland and Hachimura should lead the starters offensively.

Raphielle Johnson

Malik Monk (ankle) is doubtful for Wednesday’s game against the Clippers.

item.description:

After missing practice on Monday, Podziemski will miss Wednesday’s opener against the Lakers due to lower back soreness. However, he may not be out long, with Kerr hoping Podz can play on Friday. De’Anthony Melton is the player whose role may expand the most while Podziemski sits.

item.description:
Adou Thiero (knee) has been shut down for a few days after experiencing swelling.

Thiero will not play in Wednesday’s opener against the Warriors due to a right knee effusion. There has also been some swelling in the knee, so the Lakers are shutting the second-year wing down for a few days. Upon his clearance to resume working out, Thiero will be considered day-to-day.

Raphielle Johnson

item.title: [Injury] Deni Avdija (POR): Deni Avdija (ankle) is a game time decision against the Suns in Wednesday’s season opener.
item.description:
Deni Avdija (ankle) is a game time decision against the Suns in Wednesday’s season opener.

The Blazers already have Shaedon Sharpe out for an extended of of time. If Deni were to miss time, there would be more minutes for Sidy Cissoko and Vit Krecji, but neither would be that impactful in most fantasy leagues.

Fonte: Duane Rankin

item.title: [Injury] Cameron Carr (LAL): According to Lakers head coach JJ Redick, Cameron Carr (oblique) is “ramping up” and is day-to-day moving forward.
item.description:
According to Lakers head coach JJ Redick, Cameron Carr (oblique) is “ramping up” and is day-to-day moving forward.

Carr, who played well during Summer League, was ruled out for Wednesday’s opener with a strained oblique. The good news is that a return to action may not be far away, with the rookie now considered day-to-day, according to Redick. Carr should slide into the back end of the Lakers’ perimeter rotation once cleared to play.
